skill.name: executor-spec
skill.description: Use when architecture and design gates have passed and requirements must be written down before planning, when a spec needs a verification strategy with named evidence, or when an existing spec must be superseded because a plan already depends on it.
skill.summary: Write testable specifications, linked risk assessments, and verification strategies before implementation planning.
skill.author: atri10

security_audit.summary: Most findings are Markdown formatting, legitimate test examples, or fixed sibling references, not shell substitution, reconnaissance, or exploitable traversal. The verification example writes to predictable /tmp/b, creating a local symlink overwrite risk if copied and executed. No evidence found of credential exfiltration or prompt injection; referenced sibling helpers are outside the reviewed package.

remediation.issue: The verification example writes an HTTP response to predictable /tmp/b, which another local user could replace with a symlink.
remediation.suggestion: Use a uniquely created private temporary file, quote its path, and remove it after checking the response.

medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: curl writes to predictable /tmp/b without exclusive creation. Another local user could pre-create a symlink and redirect the write to an accessible file.

content.value_statement: Ambiguous requirements create conflicting implementations and unverifiable reviews. This skill guides linked specifications, risk assessments, and verification strategies through explicit human approval.
actual_capabilities: Draft specifications with stable requirement IDs, exact global constraints, interface references, scope exclusions, and owned questions.
Trace design candidates and architecture decisions to requirements or explicit exclusions.
Build risk assessments with failure narratives, probability ratings, mitigation links, and documented acceptance conditions.
Define verification criteria for requirements and constraints using exact procedures and observable evidence.
Review documents for ambiguity, contradictions, placeholders, coverage gaps, and inconsistent counts.
Guide specification supersession, verification relinking, and impact records for existing plans.
limitations: Full workflow operation requires companion Executor scripts, references, and initiative documents that are not included in this package.
The skill defines verification procedures; later verification must execute them before results can be claimed.
Architecture and design approvals or documented waivers are required before specification work begins.
Worked examples require adaptation to the repository; the predictable temporary-file example needs safer file handling.

use_cases.title: Prepare an implementation specification
use_cases.description: Convert approved design candidates into numbered requirements, constraints, scope exclusions, and linked acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Review delivery risks before approval
use_cases.description: Connect failure scenarios to requirements, mitigations, accepted risks, and unresolved questions before authorizing planning.

use_cases.title: Define auditable acceptance evidence
use_cases.description: Map requirements and constraints to named tests, manual steps, negative cases, boundary checks, and observable outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a first specification
prompt_templates.prompt: Use executor-spec to draft requirements from [approved design handoff] for [initiative]. Include constraints, exclusions, and owned questions. Stop for human review before planning.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: turn approved design inputs into a specification draft.

prompt_templates.title: Add a linked risk assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [draft specification] with executor-spec. Write a failure narrative, trace causes, assign mitigation links, and document accepted risks. Update affected requirements before approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: assess risks while the specification remains editable.

prompt_templates.title: Complete verification coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a verification strategy for [specification]. Cover every requirement and constraint with exact procedures and expected observations. Include rejection and boundary checks. Keep results pending.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: prepare acceptance criteria without claiming execution.

prompt_templates.title: Supersede a specification with dependent plans
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess [proposed change] against [specification] and [dependent plans]. For material changes, preserve existing IDs, draft supersession documents, relink verification, and record plan impacts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: change requirements while preserving downstream traceability.

output_examples.input: Draft acceptance requirements for placement requests that name an unknown cell.
output: Requirement R02: A request naming an unavailable cell returns HTTP 422 with the error value unknown_cell.
Observable: The response contains the required status and error value; no placement row is added.
Verification: One criterion checks the rejection response, and another checks the absence of a stored placement.
Review state: Draft awaiting explicit human approval.

output_examples.input: Assess placement latency risks before approving the specification.
output: Failure scenario: Placement latency exceeded the agreed threshold as tenant count increased.
Cause: The available-cell scan was not measured at the expected tenant scale.
Mitigation: Add a measurable latency requirement and a linked load-test criterion.
Evidence plan: Record the observed percentile latency at the specified tenant count; keep the criterion pending until execution.

output_examples.input: Change a requirement threshold after implementation plans already depend on the specification.
output: Change classification: Material because the new threshold can change implementation and review outcomes.
Document action: Create a replacement specification and preserve the previous specification body.
Traceability: Keep surviving requirement numbers and relink the verification strategy to the replacement.
Plan impact: Record which dependent plans need revision and which remain unaffected.

best_practices: Provide the approved design handoff, charter, architecture records, and interface documents before drafting requirements.
Use exact thresholds and observable outcomes, then map every requirement and constraint to verification evidence.
Review companion helpers before execution, use private temporary files, and require explicit approval before passing the phase gate.
anti_patterns: Replace missing decisions with vague terms such as appropriate, robust, or performant.
Claim tests passed when the document only defines expected evidence.
Edit material requirements in place after dependent plans exist, or treat silence as approval.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What documents does this workflow produce?
faq.answer: It guides a specification, a risk assessment, and a verification strategy with linked document and requirement identifiers.

faq.question: Does the package include the Executor helper scripts?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed package contains the skill instructions and three templates; companion scripts and contract references must be provided separately.

faq.question: Does creating verification criteria mean the tests passed?
faq.answer: No. Criteria remain pending until verification executes their procedures and records observed evidence.

faq.question: Can an approved specification be changed?
faq.answer: Material changes require supersession once dependent plans exist. Surviving requirement numbers remain stable, and affected plans receive impact records.

faq.question: Are there precautions before running example commands?
faq.answer: Review companion helpers and adapt commands to your repository. Replace the predictable temporary file with a private temporary file before execution.
